messages.author: 610676dab791d93c
messages.subject: Newbie Layering Question
parts:
I've been using ggplot2 for a week or so and have bought the ggplot2
book, but am still having some troubles.

Here is what I'm currently struggling with:

I have some stock price data that looks like this:

open high low close group date
7.2 9.2 5.3 6.0 1 2008-04-30
6.2 6.2 5.7 6.1 1 2008-04-31
6.2 6.3 5.9 5.9 1 2008-05-01
......
17.4 18.2 17.3 17.6 2 2008-04-30
18.2 19.0 18.2 19.0 2 2008-04-31
19.1 19.2 19.0 19.1 2 2008-05-01

What I'd like to do is draw six lines, three for each stock with the x
axis as the date and the price on the y axis with a line for each of
the high, low, close for each stock. The stocks are indicated by the
group variable.

About as close as I've gotten is this code:
p <- ggplot(graph_stack2, aes(x=order, y=c(L,C,H)) ) + geom_point
(size=1)
p

where I've renamed low, close, high as L,C,H. This puts points rather
than lines and can only be used on one stock at a time.

This code gives lines and the two groups, but I can only plot the
close without lines for the high and low unless I reformat the data
again.

p <- ggplot(graph_stacked, aes(x=order, y=c(L,C,H), colour=group,
group=group) ) + geom_line(size=1)

I could reformat the data to make each variable / stock combination
its own group, but the more I change the data the less useful the
graphs will be as I want to use the graphs to evaluate how well my
formulas are doing at distinguishing different types of price
movements. Thus a lot of reformatting will greatly hinder the
interactivity of trying new formulas and then visualising the
results.

I've called it a layering problem, because I suspect that I can add
the different lines onto the same graph as layers, but so far I've not
been successful in doing that. If possible, I'd like to use ggplot
rather than qplot since I understand ggplot can do everything qplot
can do and I'd rather just move straight into the more flexible tool.
Any help would be appreciated.

David

messages.author: e4aec126ff1dca22
messages.subject: Re: Newbie Layering Question
parts:
Hi David -

I think you are looking for something like this :

df <- data.frame(
  time  = rep(ISOdate(year = 2010, month = 1, day = 1:30), 2),
  group = factor(rep(1:2, each = 30)),
  close = c(cumsum(rexp(30)), cumsum(rexp(30)))
)
df$high <- 1.05 * df$close
df$low <- .95 * df$close

ggplot(aes(x = time, y = close, ymax = high, ymin = low,
  group = group), data = df) +
  geom_ribbon(alpha = 1/2) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = group))

The ribbon geom is likely preferable to two additional lines.  Does that help?

Cheers
david.
